system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Multipolarity: Tech Rivalry, Regional Wars, and Market Activism
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, dynamic system driven by an intensifying tech race (especially over AI), simultaneous regional conflicts that threaten critical energy and maritime routes, and proactive economic-state interventions that reshape markets and alliances. Major powers (US, China, Russia, regional actors) and global firms mutually adapt—escalating controls, sanctions, and defensive measures—while financial and commodity flows re-route in response. The result is higher systemic sensitivity: shocks in one domain (cyber/AI incidents, a drone strike, a currency intervention) propagate quickly across security, trade, and finance.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, major multinational corporations (especially Big Tech and energy firms), financial markets and central banks, regional military theatres and maritime chokepoints, transnational supply chains, and non-state actors (terrorist, criminal, and proxy forces) interacting across technology, economic, and security domains.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic-security system (the contemporary international order combining geopolitics, global markets, and transnational technology ecosystems).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Technology & AI Competition (platforms, models, cyber security, industrial policy)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and energy targeting
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine are locked in a sustained war that is shifting toward strategic campaigns against energy infrastructure and sanctions-evasion networks, altering European energy flows and military logistics.

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz standoff and Gulf escalation
variables.description: Iran, regional Gulf states and external powers are contesting control and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, oscillating between negotiations and coercive attacks that threaten global shipping and energy security.

variables.name: US–China technology and AI competition
variables.description: The United States and China are accelerating a high-stakes rivalry across AI, semiconductors and export controls, marked by rapid corporate investment, contested supply chains and reciprocal regulatory and sanction measures.

variables.name: Currency activism and monetary geopolitics
variables.description: Major financial actors — led by the U.S. and Japan and influential global investors — are shifting toward active currency interventions and coordinated market actions, reshaping monetary norms and cross-border capital flows.

variables.name: Alliance stress over munitions and burden sharing
variables.description: U.S. allies and security partnerships are under strain as depleted air‑defense and missile stocks, divergent political priorities, and new burden‑sharing debates force shifts in military cooperation and procurement.
